profile.behavior: Migratory and primarily arboreal. It forages deliberately among outer foliage, hopping along twigs and gleaning insects from leaves, sometimes hovering briefly; breeding birds are territorial and persistent singers.
field_marks: Compact, sparrow-sized body with a rounded head and medium-length tail
Olive-gray upperparts with a subtly grayer crown
Whitish throat and belly with a pale-yellow wash along the sides
Pale eyebrow, faint gray eye-line, and conspicuous dark eye
Fairly stout gray bill and dark gray legs
Plain, rounded wings without wing bars; square to shallow-notched tail tip
profile.habitat: Open deciduous and mixed woodland, leafy groves, woodland edges, orchards, shade trees, and isolated stands near water; it uses open woods and other wooded or shrubby habitats outside the breeding season.

findings: The primary specimen is anatomically coherent: exactly one head, one beak, one tail, two plausibly attached legs with grasping feet, and one visible near-side wing with the far-side wing naturally occluded by the lateral pose.
The detached wing and head are clearly supplementary studies and do not appear attached to the primary specimen. Both studies are well formed.

Both depicted bills are stout and consistent with the reference photographs; tracing the mandibles independently shows a slight, consistent upper-mandible tip projection rather than a reversed or exaggerated bill.

The compact body, rounded head, medium-length tail, plain rounded wing without wing bars, gray-olive upperparts, pale underparts with yellow wash, weak facial pattern, conspicuous dark eye, and dark legs agree with the supplied photographs and direct identification sources.
